I am an old man now, 62 years, and I have farmed this land for many years. My millet plot is not big, just under one hectare, and I intercrop with cowpea as my father taught me — it helps the soil and gives my family more food. I will buy small fertilizer if the subsidy reaches our village, but urea is expensive and I cannot afford much, so I will also spread the manure from my goats and sheep on the plot before the rains come. My sons help me in the field but two have gone to Kano for work, so I will hire a few young men for weeding when the rains are heavy.
